en: The Sūtra on the Golden Kanabhati Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying in the country of Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada.
The Great Dharma-Preacher, out of compassion for all sentient beings,
spoke this dhāraṇī belonging to Suvarṇakaṇapatti.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke the mantra,
saying: *Namaḥ sūtade kaṭa kaṭa tiṭha matha kṛt-ūna kṛt-ūna pañja pañja*.
1. Namo ratnatrayāya. 2. Gurubhyo namaḥ. 3. Prajñe svāhā. 4. Abhūtānām. 5. Raudracittānām. 6. Mahāyānānām. 7. Mahāsiddhīnām. 8. Svāhā.
15. *no kṣaṇe* | 16. *praguptāya me* | 17. *kuru kuru* | 18. *juru juru* | 19. *muru muru* | 20.
*namo namo* | 21. The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
This is the mantra of the Golden Kana-pati for removing obstacles and difficulties.
If sentient beings receive and uphold this mantra,
there are no dharmas they perform that will not be accomplished.
One should know that there will certainly be obstacles and hindrances;
specifically, on the second, eighth, or fifteenth day of either the waxing or waning moon.
Having smeared the ground with cow dung and prepared an altar, one performs various offerings and achieves success.
Then, Kanakapāṭī, who was golden in color, addressed the Buddha, saying,
"I shall protect those who uphold this mantra."
If there are sentient beings who uphold this mantra,
whatever that person requires— be it wealth, bedding, clothing, food and drink, gold, silver, precious gems, or male and female servants— shall never again suffer from lack or deficiency.
All mantra-dharmas shall be swiftly accomplished; they will be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
The form of this image has a human body with an elephant head and six arms.
Draw it upon white cotton cloth;
it may be carved or fashioned using white sandalwood, red sandalwood, or *kṛmighna* wood as appropriate.
Other woods are not permitted.
If using pigments, do not use hide glue;
one must use fragrant juices or juices from trees that exude sap.
His body stands upright;
his nose curves to the right;
and his upper left hand grasps a sword.
Next, the hand holds the *mudgara* (joy-mallet);
the next hand holds the sword and staff;
the next hand holds the *vajra*.
Holding the rope with his lower hands,
his body is golden in color,
and his feet tread upon a mountain of gold.
Above his head are five-colored clouds;
within the clouds are the Four Heavenly Kings and various immortals scattering flowers.
To the left is Kumāra, the Pure Army.
To the right is the Great General Āṭavaka, the Commander-in-Chief; below him,
to the left, a beautiful woman is depicted standing,
making offerings with music.
To the right are depicted four great yakṣas,
each holding weapons and bearing the heads of a half-head, a pig, an elephant, and a horse;
all are clad in tiger-skin loincloths.
When creating the image, do not allow miscellaneous people or others to see it.
Once the writing is finished,
burn incense to purify yourself and abstain from the five pungent roots.
Establish the mandala within a clean chamber;
its shape—square or circular—and its dimensions may be made according to one's preference.
Within the mandala, burn incense such as guggulu, bdellium, and aloeswood.
One should offer various kinds of sustenance, such as cakes, milk-rice, *modaka* sweets, clarified butter, honey, and fruits;
whatever is performed according to one's heart.
If there are spirits who are difficult to subdue:
Twist white thread and recite the mantra over it;
for each repetition, tie a knot until forty-nine knots are complete.
Then fasten it to the left arm.
All ghosts will be bound by a single person who upholds this [mantra].
There is no need for sexual misconduct, false speech, or deceit;
once the prohibitions are observed, one must cease consuming mustard greens, coriander, and the five pungent roots.
One must not eat.
Therefore, one enters the birth-chamber of a filial family of the color-form [realm].
This seal-dharma is universally applicable.
These methods for the Vināyakas are applicable to all general rites.
Do not associate with evil persons;
it is not an impediment to bestow them upon one's companions.
The Sūtra of the Golden Kanakapāṭi Discourse
